package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"reflect"
)

// reflect.DeepEqual over interpreter-owned values: it reads both operands
// and answers; the operands are unchanged afterwards.

type Point struct{ X, Y int }
type MySlice []int
type Nested struct {
	Name string
	Pts  []Point
	M    map[string]int
}

func double(s MySlice) MySlice {
	r := make(MySlice, len(s))
	for i, v := range s {
		r[i] = v + v
	}
	return r
}

func main() {
	arg := MySlice{1, 2, 3}
	want := MySlice{2, 4, 6}
	got := double(arg)
	fmt.Println(reflect.DeepEqual(got, want), reflect.DeepEqual(got, arg), reflect.DeepEqual(arg, MySlice{1, 2, 3}))
	a := Nested{Name: "a", Pts: []Point{{1, 2}}, M: map[string]int{"k": 1}}
	b := Nested{Name: "a", Pts: []Point{{1, 2}}, M: map[string]int{"k": 1}}
	c := Nested{Name: "a", Pts: []Point{{1, 3}}, M: map[string]int{"k": 1}}
	fmt.Println(reflect.DeepEqual(a, b), reflect.DeepEqual(a, c), reflect.DeepEqual(&a, &b))
	// Unchanged afterwards: the operands are the interpreter's own storage.
	got[0] = 9
	fmt.Println(got, arg, want, a.Pts, len(a.M))
	// Positive control: values of the dependency's own kinds.
	fmt.Println(reflect.DeepEqual([]int{1}, []int{1}), reflect.DeepEqual("x", "y"))
	os.Exit(3)
}
